overview.text: The Brown Water Snake is a large, heavy, harmless water snake of the south-eastern United States. It is often one of the commonest snakes on rivers there, and is often mistaken for a cottonmouth.

identification.text: Very heavy-bodied with a neck much narrower than the head. Brown or rusty brown with about 25 square dark blotches down the back and smaller ones on the sides; yellow belly with dark marks.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Coastal lowlands from south-eastern Virginia through the Carolinas and Georgia to Florida and west along the Gulf coast.

habitat.text: Rivers, canals, cypress creeks, swamps and streams.

reproduction.text: Mates in spring on land or on branches. The young are born alive, usually in August, 14 to 58 at a time.

recognise.text: Square dark blotches down a brown back.
Heavy body, head wider than neck.
